task.description: Hard gate on ELIXIR-DEV's implementation (commit 4efff094 on this branch, `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex`). This closes a real security-relevant BLOCKER: a definition-promotion release could previously bypass its own mandatory rehearsal gate. Verdict per invariant, INV-1..INV-8 (or however many this repo's security-invariants.md currently enumerates), APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE stated for each, against the actual diff. Pay particular attention to: (1) whether the new verify_rehearsed/2 check can be bypassed by any code path that still reaches do_apply_review/3 without going through the with-chain (e.g. a second entry point); (2) whether the plan_digest comparison for the rehearsal check reuses PromotionDigest.verify_digest/2's constant-time comparison as designed, not a raw ==, since this is a security-relevant digest check; (3) whether the new 409 error responses leak any tenant-scoped or cross-tenant information beyond what the existing :invalid_transition/:digest_mismatch 409s already leak (INV-5's cross-tenant-review-id-same-response concern, already documented in promotions.ex's moduledoc, may be relevant here too); (4) that PLATFORM_ADMIN-only access to this route is unchanged by this diff.
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable invariant given a stated verdict (PASS/FAIL) against the real diff, not a general impression
Explicit verdict on whether the new gate can be bypassed by any alternate code path
Explicit verdict on whether the digest comparison used is the constant-time one
Explicit verdict on whether the new error responses introduce any new information-disclosure surface
Explicit verdict confirming route authorization (PLATFORM_ADMIN-only) is unchanged

result.summary: Reviewed commit 4efff094's diff to lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex and lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex (git diff main...HEAD, scoped to these two files) against INV-1..INV-9. Scope test: this diff adds a new tenant-data-access path (verify_rehearsed/3 invoking Letflow.Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run/2) and new 409 error responses on a tenant-scoped route, so SECURITY-REVIEWER applies. Per-invariant verdicts: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) APPLIES -- no new/changed schema or migration in this diff, but the new call path is checked: get_latest_assertion_run/2 (lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1179) requires opts[:prefix] via Keyword.fetch! and passes it to Repo.one(query, prefix: prefix); the opts flowing into verify_rehearsed/3 are the same conn.assigns.scoped_opts threaded unchanged through apply_review/4's existing with-chain (verify_apply_digest, verify_approved already use the same opts) -- no new/alternate scoping mechanism introduced, PASS. INV-2 NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started). INV-3 NOT-APPLICABLE (S5 not started). INV-4 (secrets by reference) NOT-APPLICABLE -- no secret material touched by this diff. INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) NOT-APPLICABLE formally (S4 not started) but checked anyway per the task's own flag: a cross-tenant review_id never reaches verify_rehearsed/3 at all, because PromotionReviewStore.get_review/2 (first step of the same with-chain, unchanged by this diff) is itself prefix-scoped and returns {:error, :review_not_found} for any review_id outside the caller's tenant schema before verify_approved or verify_rehearsed ever run -- the three new 409 bodies are therefore only reachable for reviews already confirmed to belong to the caller's own tenant, so they add no new cross-tenant distinguishing signal beyond what the existing :invalid_transition/:digest_mismatch 409s already have. INV-6 (new data-access path proves scoping) APPLIES and is satisfied by the INV-1 analysis above. INV-7 (no raw SQL) APPLIES -- get_latest_assertion_run/2 uses Ecto.Query (from/where/order_by/limit) and Repo.one/2, no Repo.query or string-built SQL anywhere in the diff, PASS. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) APPLIES -- verify_rehearsed/3's case statement on get_latest_assertion_run/2's result has exactly two clauses, {:error, :not_found} and {:ok, %PromotionAssertionRun{}}, which is the function's complete declared return type (@spec on lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1175-1178 has no third variant) so no bare/partial match that can raise on realistic input, PASS. INV-9 (outbound URL SSRF) NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request in this diff. Four specific concerns from the handoff: (1) bypass -- do_apply_review/3 has exactly one call site, inside apply_review/4's single with-chain, and verify_rehearsed/2 is the fourth clause of that same chain before the do_apply_review call; grepped the whole file for do_apply_review and def apply_review, confirmed no second entry point exists -- cannot be bypassed. (2) digest comparison -- verify_rehearsed calls PromotionDigest.verify_digest(assertion_run.plan_digest, plan_digest), the same constant-time function (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest.ex:87) already used by verify_apply_digest/2 two clauses above it in the same with-chain, not a raw ==. (3) information disclosure -- the three new conflict messages are generic/static strings naming no tenant, review, or digest values, and are only reachable post-tenant-scoping as explained under INV-5 above -- no new disclosure surface. (4) route authorization -- grepped lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex for the /:id/apply route and its PLATFORM_ADMIN-only plug/catch-all (documented in the moduledoc around line 60); the diff touches only render_apply/2 error-clause additions and promotion.ex's private functions, none of the plug pipeline, route matches, or authorization catch-all -- authorization is unchanged.
